about: D31, second attempt (decision log): the paired, interleaved confirmation that was the verdict on lever 1, run before the regeneration on the 300,000-patient snapshot, by tools/benchmark_matcher.py --paired-confirm (protocol paired-interleaved-1.0) into a scratch report and committed here as it was written. The reference is main before D31's second attempt (17728fc, extracted from git); the candidate is this tree at 036fff2, whose files the artifact digests bind. The replication is the paired_confirmation of verification/matcher-comparison-report.json.
rule: Keep lever 1 only if at 14 workers the paired p95 ratio (candidate over reference) is at most 0.90 in every one of the four pairs, and the candidate's own p95 over its 14-worker runs is at most 10 s, with the maximum at most 30 s and query-process memory under 4 GB; 8 workers reported, under 10 s the stretch goal (committed in fe43d0b).

verdict.note: The p95 of 30 queries is the second-slowest query, so the per-pair and pooled ratios both rest on it (seed 26 for the reference); total time per run barely moves (ratio_total_by_repeat).

paired_confirmation.order: ABBA: the reference first in even repeats, the candidate first in odd
paired_confirmation.note: Each pair is the reference code and the candidate code run back to back, each in a fresh process with a warm pool, on the same snapshot and queries; the reference runs first in even repeats and second in odd ones (ABBA). Ratios are candidate over reference: below 1 means the candidate is faster. "total" is the sum of the per-query match seconds of one run. The absolute target is judged on the candidate's own runs in this session. The pairing cancels drift that is slow against the length of a pair (minutes); it does not cancel noise within a run, nor a difference that only one order shows (compare the reference-first and candidate-first pairs).

limitations: One machine; synthetic data replicated beyond 10,000 patients.
The pairing cancels drift slow against a pair, not noise inside a run; two pairs of each order.
The snapshot was built by this tree alone; the regeneration's scaling run rebuilt it with the same identifier.
